data.name: Wings Over Europe
data.detailed_description:
Wings Over Europe: Cold War Gone Hot lets you pilot any of the 12 most legendary Cold War fighters! Realistic air combat is waiting for you, in some of the most intense dogfights of the Cold War era. Flyable aircraft include the: F-100 Super Sabre, F-105 Thunderchief, F-4 Phantom II, F-15 Eagle, A-10 Thunderbolt II, British Hunter, and the exciting vertical take-off and landing of the Harrier "jump jet." Next generation environmental effects including volumetric clouds and state-of-the-art dynamic lighting Highly-accurate planes, weapons, flight models, and challenging enemy AI Win decorations, awards, and promotions with each successful mission.


Features:

- Engage in blood-draining, G-pulling, action-packed dogfights against 13 different types of Cold War Soviet aircraft.
- Fly era-specific aircraft through Central Europe in three epic campaigns.
- From the developers of the highly successful European Air War, Strike Fighters: Project 1, and Wings Over Vietnam.
- Random mission generator provides maximum flexibility and replayability. Campaign missions also have a different outcome each time.
- Open architecture for mod support. Download thousands of user-created skins, aircraft, terrain, missions, campaigns, and editors already available on the Internet.
- Next generation environmental effects including volumetric clouds and state-of-the-art dynamic lighting.
- Highly-accurate planes, weapons, flight models, and challenging enemy AI.
- Win decorations, awards, and promotions with each successful mission.

reviews.review:
[h1]A Great Simulator Trapped in a Terrible PC Gaming Experience[/h1]

I really wanted to like Wings Over Europe, because underneath all the technical problems, there is a genuinely good flight simulator here. Unfortunately, getting the game to actually run properly was an experience in itself.
It took me hours just to get the game running. I had to install mandatory updates from the developer's website, mess around with dgVoodoo to upgrade the rendering API, and apply various fixes and workarounds just to make a 20-year-old game playable on a modern system.
And even after all that debugging, the game is still unstable. After a few sessions, I discovered that simply pressing Escape in the middle of a game can cause it to crash. At that point, it becomes difficult to recommend the game to anyone who just wants to install it and play.

[h2]The lack of a proper tutorial is another major problem[/h2]
There is literally no meaningful in-game tutorial to help new players understand the simulator. There is a PDF manual buried somewhere in the game directory, but if it weren't for the fixes and troubleshooting I was doing, I probably would have never even known it existed.
And that's a shame, because the actual simulator is good. Once you manage to get everything working, there is a lot to appreciate here. The flight model, systems, missions, and overall simulation experience are what kept me interested despite all the frustration.
[b]*** but that's exactly the problem: getting to the good part is far too much work ***[/b]

[h2]Alternatives[/h2]
If you're looking at buying this on Steam, I honestly can't recommend it. You're better off looking at Strike Fighters 2, which is available directly from the developer and offers a more practical way to get into this style of simulation.
Another alternative worth considering is IL-2 Sturmovik: 1946, especially with the BAT (Barracuda Advanced Technologies) mod, which adds a huge amount of content and includes plenty of jet-era aircraft.

[h1]Final note[/h1]
Wings Over Europe is a good simulator buried underneath a frustrating amount of technical baggage. If you're willing to spend hours troubleshooting an old game, you might eventually get something enjoyable out of it.But if you're asking me “Should I buy this on Steam and expect it to just work?”

Absolutely not.

The simulator deserves better than the PC gaming experience surrounding it.
